cards.hypothesis: Subject-specific autonomic reactivity patterns cause non-exchangeability within Mondrian taxonomy bins, violating the conditional coverage assumption for high-reactivity individuals
cards.proposed_mechanism: High autonomic reactivity subjects exhibit EDA and HRV trajectories during stress that systematically deviate from the population-conditional distribution used to calibrate Mondrian bins, causing their nonconformity scores to fall in the tails of the calibration distribution
cards.causal_path: High trait autonomic reactivity -> amplified sympathetic response to stressor -> EDA peak amplitude and HRV suppression exceeding bin-conditional distribution -> nonconformity scores systematically larger than calibration quantile -> undercoverage
control_variables: include age_sex_BMI as covariates in reactivity score
cards.rival_explanation: Undercoverage stems from sensor artifacts in high-reactivity subjects (excessive sweating causing EDA electrode saturation) rather than true physiological non-exchangeability
cards.rival_prediction: If sensor saturation causes undercoverage, EDA signal quality indices (SQI) will correlate with coverage failure; if true non-exchangeability, SQI will be uncorrelated but reactivity score will predict coverage
cards.distinguishing_test: Compute per-subject EDA SQI (signal-to-noise ratio, saturation percentage) and test correlation with per-subject coverage deficit; simultaneously test trait reactivity score correlation. True mechanism predicts reactivity correlation > SQI correlation
cards.effect_size_rationale: Prior WESAD analyses show ~30% of subjects are high reactors with 2-3x EDA response magnitude; Mondrian binning on 10 bins yields ~10 subjects/bin; expected coverage drop from 90% to 70-75% for high-reactivity bins
minimum_data_needed: per-subject EDA time series during stress condition
per-subject HRV (RMSSD) during baseline and stress
Mondrian taxonomy bin assignments for each calibration point
nonconformity scores for each test point
cards.testable_prediction: Subjects in top tertile of trait autonomic reactivity will show empirical coverage <85% at nominal 90% level, while bottom tertile will achieve >=88%
cards.failure_condition: No significant difference in empirical coverage between high and low reactivity tertiles (p>0.05, two-proportion z-test)
cards.statistical_test_plan: Two-proportion z-test comparing coverage rates between reactivity tertiles; logistic regression of coverage indicator on continuous reactivity score with bin as random effect
cards.falsification_test: Re-calibrate Mondrian bins using only high-reactivity subjects' calibration data; if undercoverage persists, mechanism is falsified (non-exchangeability not resolved by within-group calibration)

cards.hypothesis: Wrist-worn EDA sensor displacement during stress-induced movement creates subject-specific signal degradation that Mondrian taxonomy fails to capture
cards.proposed_mechanism: Stress-induced fidgeting and gross motor movements cause wrist sensor displacement, reducing EDA signal quality in a subject-specific manner that correlates with stress intensity but is invisible to the Mondrian taxonomy which uses only feature values
cards.causal_path: Stress condition -> increased motor activity (ACC magnitude) -> wrist sensor displacement -> EDA signal attenuation/noise -> feature extraction yields biased low EDA features -> nonconformity scores miscalibrated -> undercoverage for high-movement subjects
cards.rival_explanation: Chest-worn EDA (reference) also shows undercoverage for same subjects, indicating physiological not sensor mechanism
cards.rival_prediction: If chest EDA shows same undercoverage pattern for high-movement subjects, sensor displacement is not primary cause; if chest EDA coverage is nominal, wrist displacement is implicated
cards.distinguishing_test: Compare per-subject coverage deficit between wrist-EDA-based and chest-EDA-based Mondrian predictors; test interaction: movement_level * sensor_location on coverage
cards.effect_size_rationale: WESAD wrist ACC shows 3-5x increase during stress; literature reports 15-40% EDA signal loss from displacement; expected coverage drop 10-15% for top movement quartile
minimum_data_needed: Mondrian predictions from wrist-only and chest-only features
cards.testable_prediction: Subjects in top quartile of stress-period wrist ACC magnitude will show >=12% lower coverage with wrist-EDA features vs chest-EDA features
cards.failure_condition: No significant interaction between sensor_location (wrist vs chest) and movement_level on coverage (p>0.05)
cards.statistical_test_plan: Mixed-effects logistic regression: coverage ~ sensor_location * ACC_quartile + (1|subject); test interaction term
cards.falsification_test: Apply motion artifact correction (wavelet denoising + ACC regression) to wrist EDA; if undercoverage persists identically, displacement mechanism falsified

cards.hypothesis: Delayed physiological recovery in subset of subjects creates temporal non-stationarity violating Mondrian's exchangeability assumption within calibration window
cards.proposed_mechanism: Slow physiological recovery subjects maintain elevated sympathetic activation into subsequent baseline/calibration periods, contaminating the calibration distribution with stress-residual signals that shift nonconformity score distribution
cards.causal_path: Slow recovery phenotype -> incomplete HRV/EDA recovery during post-stress baseline -> calibration set contains stress-contaminated baseline samples -> nonconformity score distribution shifted toward stress values -> test stress samples appear less anomalous -> undercoverage
control_variables: use only first baseline per session
exclude subjects with baseline HRV < 90% of pre-study baseline
cards.rival_explanation: Undercoverage occurs only for first stress trial (novelty effect), not due to recovery contamination of calibration
cards.rival_prediction: If novelty effect: undercoverage only for trial 1 regardless of recovery speed; if recovery contamination: undercoverage correlates with recovery time constant across all trials
cards.distinguishing_test: Plot per-subject coverage deficit vs HRV recovery time constant (exponential fit to post-stress HRV); test correlation. Separately test trial_number effect on coverage
cards.effect_size_rationale: WESAD has 10min inter-trial intervals; literature shows 20-30% subjects have HRV recovery >10min; expected coverage reduction 3-5% for slow recoverers
minimum_data_needed: continuous HRV (RMSSD) and EDA throughout entire protocol
cards.testable_prediction: Subjects with HRV recovery time constant >8min will show coverage deficit >=4% compared to fast recoverers (<4min), significant at p<0.05
cards.failure_condition: No correlation between HRV recovery time constant and coverage deficit (Spearman rho p>0.05)
cards.statistical_test_plan: Spearman correlation between recovery_tau and coverage_deficit; linear mixed model coverage ~ recovery_tau + trial_number + (1|subject)
cards.falsification_test: Re-run Mondrian using only calibration samples from final 5min of each baseline (maximal recovery); if undercoverage unchanged, recovery contamination mechanism falsified

cards.hypothesis: Mondrian taxonomy bins based on discrete condition labels fail to capture continuous stress intensity variation, causing undercoverage for subjects with sub-threshold stress responses
cards.proposed_mechanism: Mondrian categories use discrete condition labels (baseline/stress/amusement) but physiological stress response is continuous; subjects with weak stress responses fall in 'stress' bin but have feature distributions near baseline, inflating nonconformity scores for true stress samples
cards.causal_path: Discrete Mondrian taxonomy (condition label) -> bins contain heterogeneous stress intensities -> weak responders' stress samples resemble baseline distribution -> nonconformity scores for weak responders' stress samples exceed calibration quantile -> undercoverage
control_variables: include self_report_stress as continuous covariate in analysis
cards.rival_explanation: Undercoverage for weak responders is due to label noise (mislabeling of condition) not taxonomy granularity
cards.rival_prediction: If label noise: weak responders show random coverage pattern; if taxonomy granularity: coverage monotonically increases with stress response magnitude
cards.distinguishing_test: Bin subjects by EDA stress response magnitude (tertiles); plot coverage vs response magnitude. Test monotonic trend (Jonckheere-Terpstra). Check label consistency via video annotation for subset
cards.effect_size_rationale: WESAD self-reports show 40% of 'stress' condition subjects report low intensity; Mondrian with 3 condition bins yields high heterogeneity; expected coverage 60-70% for bottom response tertile vs 90%+ for top
cards.testable_prediction: Coverage rate will show monotonic increasing trend across EDA response magnitude tertiles (p<0.01, Jonckheere-Terpstra)
cards.failure_condition: No monotonic trend in coverage across response magnitude tertiles (p>0.05)
cards.statistical_test_plan: Jonckheere-Terpstra test for ordered alternatives across response tertiles; logistic regression coverage ~ response_magnitude + (1|subject)
cards.falsification_test: Replace discrete Mondrian taxonomy with continuous stress-intensity-stratified calibration (quantile bins of EDA response); if undercoverage eliminated for weak responders, discrete taxonomy mechanism confirmed

cards.hypothesis: Subject-specific circadian phase at testing time interacts with stress response magnitude, creating unmodeled heterogeneity in Mondrian bins
cards.proposed_mechanism: Cortisol awakening response and diurnal rhythm cause morning-tested subjects to have higher baseline cortisol and blunted stress reactivity, while afternoon subjects show larger reactivity; Mondrian bins ignore test time, mixing distinct physiological regimes
cards.causal_path: Test session time_of_day -> circadian cortisol phase -> baseline_cortisol_level -> stress_reactivity_magnitude (inverse U) -> feature distribution shift within condition bin -> nonconformity miscalibration -> undercoverage for phase-mismatched subjects
cards.rival_explanation: Time-of-day effects are mediated entirely by alertness/fatigue (PVT performance) not circadian cortisol
cards.rival_prediction: If cortisol-mediated: baseline_cortisol mediates time_of_day -> coverage relationship; if alertness-mediated: PVT reaction time mediates
cards.distinguishing_test: Mediation analysis: time_of_day -> baseline_cortisol/PVT -> coverage. Compare indirect effect sizes. Collect salivary cortisol at baseline for subset
cards.effect_size_rationale: WESAD sessions 8am-6pm; cortisol varies 50-100% across day; reactivity varies ~20%; expected coverage variation 3-5% across day
cards.testable_prediction: Subjects tested >8h after wake time will show >=4% lower coverage than those tested 2-4h after wake, controlling for sleep duration
cards.failure_condition: No significant coverage difference by time-of-day bin after controlling for sleep duration (p>0.05)
cards.statistical_test_plan: ANCOVA: coverage ~ time_of_day_bin + sleep_duration + wake_time; mediation analysis with baseline_cortisol and PVT as parallel mediators
cards.falsification_test: Re-calibrate Mondrian separately for morning (8-11am) and afternoon (2-6pm) sessions; if undercoverage persists within each stratum, circadian mechanism falsified

cards.hypothesis: Label contamination from amusement condition (physiologically similar to stress) pollutes Mondrian calibration distribution for stress class
cards.proposed_mechanism: Amusement condition in WESAD elicits sympathetic activation (laughter, arousal) overlapping with stress physiology; Mondrian taxonomy treats them as separate bins but calibration for stress bin inadvertently includes amusement-contaminated samples if label timing misaligned
cards.causal_path: Amusement condition -> sympathetic arousal (EDA/HR similar to stress) -> label transition timing error -> amusement samples enter stress calibration bin -> stress nonconformity distribution inflated -> true stress samples undercovered
control_variables: verify label timing with experiment log
cards.rival_explanation: Undercoverage is due to stress condition itself having higher variance, not amusement contamination
cards.rival_prediction: If contamination: removing transition windows improves stress coverage; if intrinsic variance: coverage unchanged after transition cleaning
cards.distinguishing_test: Re-calibrate Mondrian with increasingly strict transition exclusion windows (0s, 15s, 30s, 60s); plot stress coverage vs window size. Contamination predicts monotonic coverage improvement
cards.effect_size_rationale: WESAD condition transitions may have 10-30s labeling latency; amusement EDA overlaps stress ~40%; expected coverage recovery 5-10% with 60s exclusion
minimum_data_needed: precise condition transition timestamps from experiment log
cards.testable_prediction: Stress coverage will increase monotonically with transition exclusion window size, reaching nominal level at >=60s exclusion
cards.failure_condition: Stress coverage does not significantly improve with 60s transition exclusion vs 0s (paired McNemar p>0.05)
cards.statistical_test_plan: McNemar test comparing coverage at 0s vs 60s exclusion; linear trend test across window sizes
cards.falsification_test: Train separate Mondrian predictor using only stress condition data (no amusement in calibration); if undercoverage persists, amusement contamination mechanism falsified

cards.hypothesis: Mondrian's finite taxonomy granularity (fixed bin count) creates residual heterogeneity within bins for high-dimensional physiological feature spaces
cards.proposed_mechanism: Mondrian taxonomy uses coarse discretization (e.g., 10 bins) on high-dimensional features; subjects in tails of feature distributions within each bin have systematically different conditional distributions, violating the within-bin exchangeability assumption
cards.causal_path: High-dimensional feature space -> coarse Mondrian binning -> within-bin feature distribution heterogeneity -> tail subjects' conditional distribution differs from bin center -> nonconformity scores miscalibrated for tail subjects -> undercoverage
control_variables: use same random seed for taxonomy
cards.rival_explanation: Undercoverage is due to small calibration sample size per bin, not bin granularity per se
cards.rival_prediction: If granularity: coverage improves with more bins even at fixed sample size; if sample size: coverage improves only when samples_per_bin increases
cards.distinguishing_test: Vary Mondrian bin count (5, 10, 20, 50, 100) while holding calibration set size fixed; plot coverage vs bins. Granularity predicts improvement then plateau; sample size predicts no improvement until samples/bin > threshold
cards.effect_size_rationale: WESAD ~450 calibration samples; 10 bins = 45/bin; curse of dimensionality for 20+ features; expected coverage gain 5-8% moving from 10 to 50 bins
minimum_data_needed: full feature matrix for calibration set
Mondrian taxonomy implementation with adjustable bin count
compute infrastructure for multiple bin counts
cards.testable_prediction: Empirical coverage will increase significantly from 10 to 50 bins (p<0.01, paired test) and plateau beyond 50 bins
cards.failure_condition: No significant coverage improvement when increasing bins from 10 to 50 (p>0.05)
cards.statistical_test_plan: Repeated measures ANOVA: coverage ~ bin_count (5,10,20,50,100) + subject random effect; polynomial contrast for plateau
cards.falsification_test: Use adaptive Mondrian (k-d tree taxonomy) that creates finer bins in high-density regions; if undercoverage persists for same tail subjects, fixed granularity mechanism falsified

cards.hypothesis: Subject-specific medication or substance use (beta-blockers, SSRIs, nicotine) alters physiological stress response profile creating hidden subpopulations in Mondrian bins
cards.proposed_mechanism: Unreported medication/substance use modifies autonomic stress response (blunted HRV/EDA for beta-blockers, altered for SSRIs/nicotine); these subjects fall in same Mondrian bins as non-users but have different conditional distributions, causing miscalibration
control_variables: screen for medication/substance use via questionnaire
exclude current smokers or control cotinine
cards.rival_explanation: Observed undercoverage in medication users is due to comorbid condition physiology, not medication effect
cards.rival_prediction: If medication: coverage deficit correlates with medication class and known pharmacological effect size; if comorbidity: deficit correlates with condition severity regardless of medication
cards.distinguishing_test: Compare coverage between: (a) medicated vs unmedicated with same condition, (b) different medication classes with known autonomic effects. Use propensity matching on condition severity
cards.effect_size_rationale: Beta-blockers reduce HRV stress reactivity by 30-50%; SSRIs alter EDA; ~10-15% population on such meds; expected coverage drop 15-25% for affected subjects
cards.testable_prediction: Beta-blocker users will show coverage <=70% at nominal 90%; SSRI users <=75%; nicotine users (acute) <=80%; all significantly lower than non-users (p<0.01)
cards.failure_condition: No significant coverage difference between medication users and matched non-users (p>0.05)
cards.statistical_test_plan: Propensity score matching on age, sex, BMI, condition severity; paired McNemar test within matched pairs; ANOVA across medication classes
cards.falsification_test: Re-calibrate Mondrian excluding all medication users; if undercoverage pattern shifts to different subjects, medication mechanism confirmed; if same subjects remain undercovered, mechanism falsified

cards.hypothesis: Non-stationary sensor drift during long WESAD sessions causes time-dependent feature distribution shift that Mondrian's static calibration cannot capture
cards.proposed_mechanism: Wrist sensor (Empatica E4) exhibits baseline drift in EDA and temperature over 60-90min sessions; Mondrian calibration uses early-session data but test predictions occur later, creating temporal distribution shift within bins
cards.causal_path: Session_duration -> sensor_baseline_drift (EDA, TEMP) -> feature_distribution_shift_over_time -> calibration_distribution (early) != test_distribution (late) -> nonconformity_scores_miscalibrated_for_late_trials -> undercoverage_in_late_trials
cards.rival_explanation: Late-trial undercoverage is due to subject fatigue/habituation reducing stress response, not sensor drift
cards.rival_prediction: If sensor drift: synthetic drift added to early trials replicates late-trial coverage pattern; if fatigue: self-report fatigue correlates with coverage deficit
cards.distinguishing_test: Simulate sensor drift by adding empirically measured drift function to early-trial features; re-run Mondrian and compare coverage pattern to actual late trials. Also correlate self-report fatigue with coverage
cards.effect_size_rationale: E4 EDA drift ~0.01-0.05 μS/min; over 90min = 1-4 μS shift; typical stress response 2-10 μS; expected coverage drop 2-4% for last trial vs first
cards.testable_prediction: Coverage will decline linearly with trial index (slope < -0.5% per trial, p<0.05); adding measured drift to early trials replicates late-trial coverage
cards.failure_condition: No significant linear trend of coverage across trial index (p>0.05); drift simulation does not replicate pattern
cards.statistical_test_plan: Linear mixed model: coverage ~ trial_index + (1|subject); equivalence test between drift-simulated and actual late-trial coverage patterns
cards.falsification_test: Re-calibrate Mondrian using only late-session calibration data (matching test distribution); if undercoverage eliminated, drift mechanism confirmed; if persists, falsified

cards.hypothesis: Mondrian's assumption of exchangeability within bins fails for subjects with atypical physiological baselines (e.g., hyperhidrosis, autonomic neuropathy) creating systematic outliers
cards.proposed_mechanism: Subjects with clinical/subclinical autonomic conditions have baseline physiology outside population norms; Mondrian bins assign them based on condition label but their feature distributions are shifted, causing nonconformity scores to systematically exceed calibration quantiles
control_variables: screen for hyperhidrosis (HDSS>=3) and neuropathy (symptom questionnaire)
measure skin conductance level at rest pre-session
cards.rival_explanation: Atypical baselines are captured by Mondrian taxonomy if features include baseline values; undercoverage is due to stress-response atypicality not baseline
cards.rival_prediction: If baseline-driven: coverage correlates with baseline atypicality; if stress-response-driven: coverage correlates with stress reactivity residual after controlling baseline
cards.distinguishing_test: Compute Mahalanobis distance of baseline features from population mean; test correlation with coverage deficit. Compare to correlation with stress-reactivity residual (stress - baseline)
cards.effect_size_rationale: Hyperhidrosis prevalence ~3%; autonomic neuropathy ~2%; these subjects have 2-5 SD baseline shifts; expected coverage <50% for affected vs 90% nominal
cards.testable_prediction: Subjects screening positive for hyperhidrosis or autonomic neuropathy will show coverage <=60% (p<0.001 vs screen-negative)
cards.failure_condition: No significant coverage difference between screen-positive and screen-negative subjects (p>0.05)
cards.statistical_test_plan: Fisher's exact test for coverage <80% in screen-positive vs negative; logistic regression coverage ~ screen_status + baseline_Mahalanobis
cards.falsification_test: Re-calibrate Mondrian using subject-specific baseline normalization (z-score within subject); if undercoverage eliminated for screen-positive subjects, baseline mechanism confirmed; if persists, falsified
